English: Camel Post
A simple waystation marked by tethered camels and rough tents, serving as the first gathering point for traders and travelers on the steppes.
Merchants Tent
A hardy canvas tent where goods are bartered and traveling merchants rest, attracting small-scale trade to the caravanserai.
Pack Animal Shelter
Makeshift wooden pens and windbreaks for the protection and care of pack animals, increasing the capacity for trade caravans.
Walled Pavilion
A large, semi-permanent pavilion with low defensive walls, offering greater shelter for travelers and protection for goods.
Market Room
A timbered market hall within the caravanserai, allowing for organized trade, storage, and increased economic activity for passing caravans.
Trade Hall
A permanent, stone-built hall for merchants and travelers, bustling with trade and commerce, and reinforcing the caravanserais central role in nomadic exchange.
Camel Stable
Large, well-built stables for camels and horses, allowing for the maintenance of larger, healthier herds and swifter caravans.
Merchants House
A fortified residence for wealthy merchants, attracting influential traders and increasing the prestige and wealth of the settlement.
Storage Pavilion
A vast covered structure designed to securely hold the wealth and goods of passing caravans, enabling further expansion of trade and population.
Muslim Grand Caravanserai
A monumental stone caravanserai with ornate courtyards, mosques, and bustling markets. This grand center of commerce and faith cements the region as a hub of Islamic trade, unity, and prosperity.
